summary_markdown: The conversation covered two main technical topics. First, [p1] inquired about the availability of general logarithmic functions (base other than natural or binary) within ClickHouse; it was noted that while standard SQL supports `log(base, number)`, ClickHouse simplifies this to `ln()`. Second, [p1] encountered an issue where forecast data continued to aggregate even after removing specific companies from the query. It was determined that to correctly compare historical data with forecasts on a test dataset, the query must include an explicit condition (`is_fake=0`) applied both to the sessions and the prediction calculation itself.
decisions: The forecast calculation needs to be rerun/adjusted using `is_fake=0` for accurate comparison against historical session data.
action_items: [p1] will modify the query to include `is_fake=0` conditions on both sessions and predictions.
